title: Reduce bridge reliance on passive callbacks and derived state
description:
The bridge currently does meaningful work on passive callbacks (`GAME_UPDATE`, `GAME_UPDATE_AND_INFORM`, `CHATMESSAGE`) instead of treating decision callbacks as the only authoritative driver for MCP behavior.

Today the passive path updates `lastGameView`, advances `RoundTracker`, buffers unseen chat, rewrites turn log messages using `lastGameView`, wakes blocked MCP tools via `actionLock.notifyAll()`, and now also participates in `stack_resolved` completion by letting the wait loop observe state changes that arrived without a new actionable callback.

It is not clear that all of this belongs in the bridge. A cleaner architecture may be for the server or observer/export pipeline to track every state change, while the bridge only responds to callbacks that actually require or unblock player decisions.

Questions to answer:
- Which passive callback side effects are truly required for correct bridge behavior versus just convenient derived state?
- Can `pass_priority`/`get_action_choices` be driven entirely from actionable callbacks plus explicit tool calls, eliminating or minimizing passive wakeups?
- If `stack_resolved` remains supported, should it be redesigned around a specific watched stack object ID (for example the bottom object on the stack at tool entry) rather than polling shared passive state?
- Can chat buffering, turn rewriting, and other non-decision bookkeeping move out of the bridge entirely?

Suggested scope: audit every passive callback effect in `BridgeCallbackHandler`, classify each as required / movable / removable, then simplify the bridge toward decision-driven behavior. If some existing MCP tool semantics fundamentally require passive observation, document that explicitly instead of letting the dependency remain implicit.
